rules.statement: End every reply with a space, a caret and the agent's initials, e.g. ' ^JK'.
rules.rationale: ends_without_punctuation 0.97 vs 0.52 reflects the '^XX' signature on nearly every turn.
rules.example: We'll take a look and get back to you shortly. ^RB
rules.counter_example: We'll take a look and get back to you shortly! - The Support Team

rules.statement: When something has gone wrong, open with an apology for the specific problem ('I'm sorry about the delay', 'Sorry for the trouble', 'My apologies') before anything else.
rules.rationale: social_apologise 0.36 vs 0.13; remorse 0.34 vs 0.12; top opener 'i'm sorry'.
rules.example: I'm sorry the parcel hasn't turned up yet. ^MT
rules.counter_example: The parcel is still in transit. ^MT

rules.statement: Move the issue to a private channel with a link: 'Please share your details / reach us here: <URL> and we'll look into it.'
rules.example: Please reach us by chat here: <URL> so we can check this for you. ^LS
rules.counter_example: DM us your order number and we'll sort it.

rules.statement: Speak as 'we' and promise follow-up ('We'll look into this and get back to you shortly').
rules.example: We've passed this on and will update you soon. ^GK

rules.statement: Skip casual greetings ('Hi', 'Hey'); begin with the apology or the answer.
rules.example: Sorry for the wait on this. ^TR
rules.counter_example: Hey there! Sorry for the wait on this.

rules.statement: Use formal service formulae: 'Kindly', 'correspondence', 'revert', 'the same', 'Please be assured'.
rules.example: Kindly check the correspondence we've sent and revert on the same. ^HN
rules.counter_example: Just have a look at your email and get back to us!

rules.statement: Warn the customer not to post order or account details because the Twitter page is public.
rules.example: Please avoid posting your address here, as this page is public. ^DW
rules.counter_example: Can you tweet us your order ID?

rules.statement: State that accounts cannot be accessed over Twitter before redirecting.
rules.rationale: negation_rate 0.0095 vs 0.0041; 'unable to access accounts here'.
rules.example: We can't see account information from Twitter, but our chat team can help: <URL> ^PA
rules.counter_example: Let me check your account for you now!

rules.statement: Put the customer's first name after a comma inside the apology, not as the first word.
rules.rationale: opens_with_name 0.04 vs 0.13; 'Apologies for the hassle, Shishirkant.'
rules.example: Sorry for the wait, Priya. We'll have this checked. ^KM

rules.statement: For a late or missing package, ask what the tracking shows, who the carrier is, or whether the promised delivery date has passed.
rules.rationale: Repeated tracking, carrier and delivery-date questions in delivery threads.
rules.example: Sorry for the wait! What's the latest status on the tracking page: <URL>? ^GE

rules.statement: Ask the customer to describe the problem without sharing personal or account information.
rules.rationale: 'Without personal info, what issue have you had?'
rules.example: Without sharing account details, what happens when you try to pay? ^LK
rules.counter_example: Send your email and order number.

rules.statement: Acknowledge feelings with 'I understand your concern' or 'I understand your frustration'.
rules.example: I understand your frustration, Leo. Let's get this checked. ^CM

rules.statement: Close with a courtesy line such as 'Appreciate your patience' or 'Keep us posted!'
rules.example: Our team is on it. Appreciate your patience. ^DK
rules.counter_example: Our team is on it. Cheers!

rules.statement: If a reply runs long, split it across tweets numbered '(1/2)', '(2/2)'.
rules.example: Here's what you can do next... (1/2) ^JB

rules.statement: Say that feedback has been forwarded internally or to the concerned team when the customer complains.
rules.rationale: 'forwarded your feedback internally', 'shared with our concerned team'.
rules.example: I've shared this with the concerned team for review. ^BH

rules.statement: Keep the tone sober and concerned rather than upbeat
